summary: 有些鸟须模仿才能唱出成鸟的歌，另一些则能天生发出本物种的鸣声。研究者考察习得歌声的脑区与演化来源，并讨论复杂鸟鸣在适应栖息地、吸引配偶和暴露于捕食者之间的权衡。
logic: 幼鸟如何学唱，哪些鸣声是天生的
学唱涉及哪些脑区，它们如何演化
环境与择偶如何影响鸟类的歌声
醒目的歌声也会引来捕食者

paragraphs.brief: 红雀春鸣展示罕见的学习本领
sentences: Like an apple bough bursting with fragrant blossoms, a cardinal crooning loudly from the treetops is a sure sign of spring.
苹果枝头绽放的香花预示着春天，树梢上高声歌唱的红雀也是如此。
But the bird also is displaying a highly unusual talent.
但鸟也表现出了一种非常不寻常的天赋。
Cardinals, along with other songbirds, are among the few kinds of animals that learn the vocalizations they make.
红雀和其他鸣禽属于少数能够学习自身发声方式的动物。
Among the others, two groups are also birds—hummingbirds and parrots—and the rest are mammals: bats, cetaceans, elephants and humans.
其它的还有两组鸟类——蜂鸟和鹦鹉——其余是哺乳动物：蝙蝠、鲸目动物、大象和人类。
All other creatures, from dogs and tigers to swans, owls and pigeons, produce sounds that, according to current research, are programmed by the species’ genes.
按照目前的研究，其他动物从狗、老虎到天鹅、猫头鹰和鸽子，发出的声音都是由本物种的基因预先决定的。
“Not even the chimpanzee, our closest living relative, is a vocal learner,” says Erich Jarvis, a Duke University Medical Center neurobiologist who studies the trait.
研究这种能力的杜克大学医学中心神经生物学家埃里希·贾维斯说：“就连与我们亲缘关系最近的现生动物黑猩猩，也不会学习发声。”
paragraphs.gist: 红雀在树梢高唱是春天的标志，也展示了少数动物才有的本领：从别的个体那里学习发声，连与人类亲缘最近的黑猩猩也做不到。

paragraphs.brief: 幼鸟学唱与婴儿学语相似
sentences: According to Jarvis and other scientists, baby songbirds learn to sing much like human infants learn to speak.
据贾维斯和其他科学家说，婴儿歌鸟学会唱歌，就像人类婴儿学会说话。
Both begin by listening to their parents or other adults and memorizing the sounds.
两者起初都先听父母或其他成年个体发声，再把听到的声音记住。
The next step is to mimic the mentors, slowly perfecting their “language” over time through practice.
下一步是模仿导师，通过实践逐渐完善他们的“语言”。

“I love hearing the similarities between a babbling baby bird and a babbling baby human,” says biologist Donald Kroodsma, a retired professor at the University of Massachusetts and author of the book The Singing Life of Birds.
马萨诸塞大学退休教授、《鸟类的歌唱生活》作者唐纳德·克鲁兹马说：“我很喜欢听雏鸟试唱和婴儿咿呀学语之间的相似之处。”
“Each takes bits and pieces of the sounds adults produce, repeating them in completely random sequences until the proper vocalization takes shape.”
“它们都从成年个体的声音中取出片段，按完全随机的顺序反复练习，直到正确的发声逐渐成形。”
paragraphs.gist: 雏鸟学唱与婴儿学说话相似，都先听成年个体发声，再反复模仿，最初散乱的声音片段才逐渐组合成正确的表达。

paragraphs.brief: 异种抚养区分先天与后天鸣声
sentences: Like a French child raised by English-speaking parents, a young songbird raised by a different species of adult, or with recordings of a different species, will end up learning the “wrong” song—and will produce only an odd, improvised tune if it is raised in isolation.
就像由说英语的父母养大的法国孩子，雏鸟若由异种成鸟抚养或只听异种录音，最终就会学会“错的”歌；若独自长大，只会发出古怪的即兴曲调。
A vocal nonlearner such as a phoebe or a dove, on the other hand, will sing its species’ correct song even if it’s brought up by another kind of bird, or by none at all.
相反，菲比霸鹟或鸽子不靠后天学习发声，即使由别种鸟抚养，甚至没有成鸟带大，也会发出本种正确的鸣声。
paragraphs.gist: 需要学唱的鸣禽会跟着异种成鸟学出别种歌声，孤立饲养也唱不正常；东菲比霸鹟或鸽子却不必学也能叫出本种的声音。

paragraphs.brief: 鸟鸣方言与学唱年龄限制
sentences: For songbirds, the final stage of learning often takes place once a fledgling leaves its parents’ territory.
对于小鸟来说，学习的最后阶段往往在幼鸟离开父母领地时进行。
After settling in a new location, the bird may incorporate into its own repertoire local variations on the species’ song.
幼鸟在新地点定居后，可能会把当地同种鸟鸣唱的变体纳入自己的曲目。
“Just like people, songbirds have dialects,” says Kroodsma, who has studied bird songs for more than three decades.
研究鸟鸣三十多年的克鲁兹马说：“鸣禽和人一样，也有方言。”
He has discovered that black-capped chickadees on Martha’s Vineyard, for example, have different dialects than chickadees in the rest of Massachusetts.
例如，他发现玛莎葡萄园岛上黑顶山雀的“方言”，与马萨诸塞州其他地方的同种鸟不同。
The same is true of white-crowned sparrows in California, which produce markedly different songs from sparrows just a few miles up or down the coast.
加利福尼亚的白冠带鹀也是如此，沿海岸相距仅几英里的鸟，唱腔就可能明显不同。
Like most people, who after adolescence have difficulty learning foreign languages, most songbirds lose the ability to learn new melodies after they reach maturity.
像大多数人一样，在青春期后难以学习外语，大多数歌鸟在成熟后丧失学习新旋律的能力。
A handful of species, however—including mynas, mockingbirds and starlings—are able to pick up new tunes throughout their lives.
不过，八哥、嘲鸫和椋鸟等少数鸟类一生都能学会新的曲调。
paragraphs.gist: 幼鸟离开亲鸟后还能学当地“方言”，沿海相隔几英里的白冠雀就会唱得不同；多数鸣禽成年便不再学新曲，少数则能终身学习。

paragraphs.brief: 三个远缘鸟群的脑区相似
sentences: A few years ago, Jarvis and his colleagues made the surprising discovery that when a songbird, parrot or hummingbird is producing its learned vocalization, a set of seven similar structures in the birds’ brains become active.
贾维斯和同事发现，鸣禽、鹦鹉或蜂鸟发出后天学来的声音时，脑内一组相似的七处结构都会变得活跃。
The finding was unexpected because the three avian groups are only distantly related to one another.
这个发现出人意料，因为这三类鸟彼此的亲缘关系都很远。
At the same time, they are closely related to other birds that are not vocal learners.
与此同时，它们各自却有不会学习发声的鸟类近亲。
Flycatchers, for example, belong to the same order as songbirds—Passeriformes—yet no flycatcher species tested so far displays the trait.
例如，捕蝇鸟与鸣禽同属雀形目，但迄今测试过的捕蝇鸟没有一个物种表现出这种能力。
paragraphs.gist: 鸣禽、鹦鹉和蜂鸟发出学来的声音时，脑内七处相似结构都会活跃，这令人意外，因为三类鸟亲缘较远，有些近亲反而不会学唱。

paragraphs.brief: 共同祖先或独立演化的假说
sentences: One possible explanation, says Jarvis, is that the three groups of vocal learning birds had a common ancestor that possessed the skill.
贾维斯说，一个可能的解释是，三个声音学习的鸟类组有一个共同的祖先拥有这个技能。
“But this means there would have been multiple losses of the ability over time, a sort of mass extinction of vocal learning,” he says.
他说：“但那就意味着，在漫长的演化过程中这种能力曾多次消失，仿佛发声学习能力经历过一次大灭绝。”

Another hypothesis is that vocal learners evolved similar brain structures independently over the last 65 million years, much the same way that birds and bats separately evolved wings that turned out to be so much alike.
另一种假说是，在过去六千五百万年里，会学习发声的动物各自演化出了相似的脑结构，就像鸟和蝙蝠分别演化出了十分相像的翅膀一样。
paragraphs.gist: 三类鸟的相似能力有两种可能解释：共同祖先早已会学唱，后来许多后代失去它，或者它们像鸟和蝙蝠各自长出翅膀那样独立演化。

paragraphs.brief: 人脑线索与运动学习系统
sentences: Discoveries about the human brain support this latter hypothesis.
人类大脑的发现支持了后一种假设。
Scientists conducting imaging studies have found that when people speak, parts of their brains’ cerebrums that are similar to those of vocalizing songbirds, parrots and hummingbirds become active.
脑成像研究发现，人说话时，大脑中一些区域会变得活跃，这些区域与鸣禽、鹦鹉和蜂鸟发声时活跃的区域相似。
They’ve also found that the same neural pathways are damaged in people who have lost the ability to speak due to injury or stroke.
他们也发现同样的神经路径在因受伤或中风而失去说话能力的人身上遭到破坏。

Jarvis now believes that vocal learning most likely developed independently in humans and the three bird groups (as well as in other learners whose brains have not been studied)—yet it arose from a preexisting brain system, probably shared by all vertebrates, that controls learning to move.
贾维斯如今认为，人类、这三类鸟和其他尚未研究过脑结构的发声学习者，很可能各自演化出了发声学习能力，但都借用了已有的运动学习系统，而这套系统或为所有脊椎动物所共有。
paragraphs.gist: 人说话时活跃的脑区与鸟学鸣时的脑区相似，贾维斯认为人和鸟可能分别利用原有的运动学习系统，独立演化出了发声学习能力。

paragraphs.brief: 鸟类回路研究的临床潜力
sentences: However vocal learning evolved, Jarvis and other scientists say that a better understanding of how birds learn to sing should provide insight into human language acquisition, as well as potential new treatments for speech disorders.
贾维斯和其他科学家表示，更深入地了解鸟类如何学会唱歌，就能深入了解人类语言的学习，以及潜在的新治疗语言障碍的方法。
“The clinical implications are significant,” he says.
他说，“临床影响是重大的”。
“If we can learn how to repair damaged vocal-learning circuits in the songbird brain, there’s a good chance we can learn how to repair them in humans as well.”
“如果能弄清怎样修复鸣禽脑中受损的发声学习回路，我们也很可能找到修复人类相应回路的方法。”
paragraphs.gist: 研究鸟如何学唱，有望帮助理解人类习得语言的过程，若能修复鸣禽受损的发声学习回路，或许也能为人类言语障碍治疗提供线索。

paragraphs.brief: 不同栖息环境需要不同鸣声
sentences: Biologists have proposed at least two reasons why vocal learning—and the complex vocalizations it generates—would be favored during a species’ evolution.
对于发声学习及其产生的复杂叫声为何能在物种演化中得到保留，生物学家提出了至少两条理由。
One advantage is that the trait provides flexibility to animals that must communicate across a variety of habitat types.
其中一个优点是，这种特性为动物提供了灵活性，它们必须跨越各种生境类型进行交流。

While vocal-nonlearning doves don’t need to adjust their simple, low-frequency calls that travel so well along the ground—nor flycatchers their high-pitched songs that pass best through the air—most songbirds move in and out and throughout the layers of a forest, requiring a larger repertoire of sounds.
鸽子不必调整贴近地面也传得很远的低频鸣声，捕蝇鸟也无需调整最适合在空中传播的高音，但在林间各层穿行的多数鸣禽需要储备更多种声音。
Jarvis points out that Homo sapiens evolved in East Africa’s Rift Valley, a region where a variety of habitats also occur within short distances of one another.
贾维斯指出，智人是在东非裂谷进化而成的，在这个区域，各种生境也发生在彼此的很近的距离内。
paragraphs.gist: 发声学习的一个优势是可以适应不同栖息环境：在森林各层穿行的鸣禽需要多种声音，而只在特定环境传声的鸟未必需要改变叫声。

paragraphs.brief: 雌鸟择偶偏好复杂歌声
sentences: But an even stronger selection pressure for vocal learning, say biologists, is mate attraction.
生物学家认为，吸引配偶可能是推动发声学习演化的更强选择压力。

Scientists studying several songbird species have demonstrated that females prefer males that produce the most complex songs—or, as Jarvis puts it, “The more variability in your vocalizations, the sexier you are.”
研究几类歌鸟的科学家已经证明，雌鸟更喜欢制作最复杂的歌曲的雄鸟，或者，正如贾维斯所说的那样，“你的发声越多变，你就越性感。”
paragraphs.gist: 雌鸟在多个鸣禽物种中偏爱歌曲更复杂的雄鸟，因此吸引伴侣可能比适应环境更有力地推动了学唱能力的演化。

paragraphs.brief: 雄鸟唱功、脑结构与遗传
sentences: Other research, showing a link between a male bird’s song and his genetic fitness, suggests that the females know what they are doing.
其他研究显示，雄鸟的歌声与其基因健康有联系，表明雌鸟知道自己在做什么。

In a laboratory study of sedge warblers and zebra finches, for example, Cornell University psychologist and neurobiologist Timothy DeVoogd discovered that a male’s superior singing skills correlate with larger brain structures—and that among zebra finches, these bigger brains are inherited by the birds’ sons.
康奈尔大学的蒂莫西·德沃格德研究水蒲苇莺和斑胸草雀后发现，雄鸟歌唱本领出众与某些脑结构较大有关，斑胸草雀还会把脑较大的特点遗传给雄性后代。
“If you’re picking a male with a fancier song,” says DeVoogd, “you’re probably also picking one who’s a little bit smarter.”
德沃格德说：“雌鸟选择歌声较复杂的雄鸟，可能也就选中了更聪明一点的伴侣。”
paragraphs.gist: 在莺和斑胸草雀中，雄鸟唱得好与某些脑结构较大相关，斑胸草雀还能把这一特点遗传给雄性后代，使雌鸟择偶偏好显得有据可循。

paragraphs.brief: 早年压力与模仿歌曲的表现
sentences: In another study, Duke biologist Stephen Nowicki tested the response of female song sparrows to captive males whose abilities to accurately copy the songs of wild birds varied.
杜克大学生物学家斯蒂芬·诺维茨基研究了雌性歌带鹀对圈养雄鸟的反应，这些雄鸟准确模仿野外鸟鸣的能力各不相同。
As expected, he observed that females favored males that more accurately copied wild-type songs.
正如预期，雌鸟更喜欢能够更准确模仿野外歌声的雄鸟。
But more significantly, Nowicki also discovered that birds with inferior songs had experienced stress early in life, which he suggests may have hampered brain development.
更重要的是，诺维茨基发现唱得较差的鸟在幼年经历过压力，他认为这些压力可能妨碍了大脑发育。
paragraphs.gist: 雌性歌带鹀更喜欢准确模仿野外歌曲的雄鸟，学得较差的雄鸟幼年曾遭受压力，研究者推测那段经历可能影响了脑发育。

paragraphs.brief: 引来捕食者可能限制学唱
sentences: Given such clear advantages, why is it that so few animal species are vocal learners?
既然学习发声的优势如此明显，为何能掌握这种本领的动物物种却很少？
To most biologists, the answer remains a fascinating mystery.
对多数生物学家来说，答案仍是个引人入胜的谜。
Jarvis, however, has his own idea: “Species have a strong potential to develop vocal learning,” he says, “but something is also selecting against it, and I think that something is predators.”
贾维斯有自己的解释：“物种有很大潜力演化出发声学习能力，但同时也有一种选择压力不利于这种能力，我想那就是捕食者。”
Like a peacock’s elaborate tail or a tanager’s dazzling colors, complex vocalizations may attract females, he suggests, but predators notice them, too.
他认为，复杂的鸣声与孔雀华丽的尾羽或唐纳雀耀眼的羽色一样，固然可能吸引雌性，却也会引起捕食者的注意。
paragraphs.gist: 善于学唱的物种终究很少，贾维斯推测，复杂的叫声虽然吸引配偶，也会暴露在捕食者耳中，这种风险可能抵消了优势。

paragraphs.brief: 顶着捕食风险歌唱的信号
sentences: Following that logic, a bright red cardinal singing boldly from a treetop may indeed make a worthy mate.
照这个逻辑推想，一只通体鲜红、敢在树梢高歌的红雀，或许确实是值得选择的伴侣。
After all, says Jarvis, “The better you sing your song, the more attention you’ll get.
贾维斯说：“毕竟，唱得越好，你吸引的注意就越多。
And if you can do that and also escape predation, you must be a pretty good animal.”
要是既能做到这一点，又能逃脱捕食，你的生存本领一定相当不错。”
paragraphs.gist: 树梢上的红雀越会唱越惹人注目，如果仍能逃过捕食，这种在危险中展示本领的表现本身就可能说明它是好伴侣。
